status: Referentenentwurf (draft bill) — consultation closed 22.05.2026, cabinet decision pending
highlights: § 184k StGB fully rewritten: producing AND distributing intimate imagery punishable, real or deepfake, private or public location — up to 2 years or fine. Covers pornographic deepfakes, public sauna/changing-room/beach voyeurism, clothed intimate body parts 'in sexually determined manner', revenge porn, non-consensual sharing of sexting material.

New § 201b StGB: unauthorised making-available (not production) of reputation-damaging non-sexual deepfakes, incl. of deceased persons; satire excluded. Precursor was Bundesrat proposal BT-Drs. 21/1383.

New § 202e StGB: repeated/continuous unauthorised surveillance of location or activities via IT/communication tech (GPS trackers, spyware) — up to 2 years or fine; only if likely to cause serious harm. Lowers the § 238 StGB evidentiary hurdle for stalkerware cases.

Civil enforcement package: extended right to information about infringer identity (judicial approval), evidence-preservation orders against platforms, temporary court-ordered account suspension, mandatory domestic authorised recipient for non-EU social networks.
German draft goes beyond EU Directive 2024/1385 (which only requires criminalising distribution); EU transposition deadline mid-2027.
No changes detected to §§ 185/186/187, § 241, § 238 wording, §§ 303a/303b, § 201a wording. No new BNetzA harassment-related enforcement rules found.
